candidate.claim: Auditing/filtering benchmark tasks can reverse model rankings even when the exact same stored trajectories are re-scored.

same_trajectory_design.detail: eval_splits.md defines Filtering as re-scoring the same Original trajectories on the surviving task set after dropping every flagged non-KEEP task (FIX ∪ REMOVE ∪ TODO); it explicitly says no reruns and original data. Fixed is a different variant that applies repairs/reruns where required.

overall_leaderboard.aggregation: leaderboard/README.md states equal-weight macro-average over the seven live benchmark keys, restricted to models present in all of them

scope_clarifications: The result directly establishes ranking sensitivity to the AgentSuite audit/filtering policy on committed stored trajectories; it does not establish that every dropped task is objectively invalid.

Filtering drops FIX and TODO tasks in addition to REMOVE tasks. FIX means correctable, TODO means unresolved, and REMOVE means unfixable/invalid. Therefore downstream wording should prefer 'audit-flagged task composition' or 'Filtering policy' over treating the entire dropped set as proven-invalid tasks.

Because Filtering performs no rerun, this experiment isolates denominator/task-set re-scoring on stored trajectories. It does not measure behavior after repaired wording/data/environment changes; that belongs to Fixed.
Some per-benchmark rows can have partial coverage. The cited tau-bench reversal uses full-coverage rows with n_all=165, n_filtered=139 and all 26 filter IDs matched.
The current public leaderboard documents Original/Filtering only; Fixed leaderboard results are not live, so FE-021 does not support Fixed-vs-Filtering causal attribution.

corrections.from: This directly demonstrates benchmark-task validity as a possible source of ranking instability.
corrections.to: This directly demonstrates that AgentSuite's audit-flagged task composition / Filtering policy can be a source of ranking instability on the same stored trajectories. It is not proof that every filtered task was invalid.

confidence: high for committed split semantics and rank/score values; no independent trajectory recomputation performed in this audit
unresolved: Fixed-vs-Filtering attribution: quantify how much score/rank change comes from deleting flagged tasks versus repairing FIX tasks and rerunning them once provenance-equivalent Fixed results become available.
Independent recomputation from the referenced stored trajectory datasets was not performed here; this audit verifies the committed primary repository semantics and computed CSV outputs.
downstream_instruction: Evidence comparator/integrator may retain FE-021 as same-trajectory benchmark-composition ranking sensitivity, but must use the scope clarification above and must not label all filtered tasks invalid or infer Fixed behavior from Filtering.
